subject.title: Hardcoded 300s per-chat queue timeout with no configuration or lifecycle hooks

question: Should Feishu expose a plugin-scoped queue-timeout setting and explicit progress behavior, or should long-running-turn acknowledgement and completion ordering be designed as a shared channel contract first?
rationale: The source confirms the fixed timeout and continuation behavior, but choosing whether progress and asynchronous completion belong to Feishu alone or to the channel framework determines the permanent API and configuration surface.

options.title: Start with a Feishu-scoped policy
options.body: Add a bounded, account-inheritable timeout setting plus documented progress behavior while retaining the existing five-minute default and queue safety semantics.

options.title: Design a shared channel contract
options.body: Define portable acknowledgement, completion, and ordering semantics before adding hooks or asynchronous delivery behavior to Feishu.

options.title: Keep the fixed policy
options.body: Retain the present safety cap and rely on existing typing and streaming feedback without exposing a timeout control.

recommendation.title: Start with a Feishu-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Add a bounded, account-inheritable timeout setting plus documented progress behavior while retaining the existing five-minute default and queue safety semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested configuration and user-visible behavior are owned by the Feishu plugin surface.
